chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza and others, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the roof upon which one sleeps, and it is not enclosed (by a boundary wall), he (peace be upon him) said: 'It suffices for him if the height of the wall is two cubits.'

key_terms.السَّطْح: Roof or flat surface of a building

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum required height for a wall enclosing a roof in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This ruling from al-Kafi addresses the technical requirements for a roof (sath) to be considered a valid private space (hujrah) for prayer or residence, specifically when it lacks a fully enclosed perimeter. The specification of a two-cubit wall height reflects the practical architectural norms of early Islamic Medina, balancing privacy needs with structural simplicity. It underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that legal definitions of domestic spaces are often calibrated to contemporary living conditions to ensure ritual validity.
